Next I'll move the non-MVM work off the CPU: attention and softmax to the vector-unit path, vector ops to the VFU, and lm_head to the crossbar. I'm also trimming xbar_scale to 1.0 and using a moderate VFU (16 lanes, 256 GB/s, 16 GB) to keep area under 3000 mm2.

Eval #3 moved attention, softmax, vector, and lm_head off the CPU and improved time by only 2%, so the remaining bottleneck is probably the CPU-coprocessor link rather than compute. I'll keep #3's design and change only link to 'die' to test that directly. If time drops a lot, the link is the limit; if not, the next step is kv_bits or edge.

Designs so far differ by under 3%, so the bottleneck is likely in the CPU-side attention, softmax, or elementwise ops that the small VFU barely touches. Next I'll move attention into crossbars with the transpose flavor (cheap K append), put softmax on the star unit, and send edge work to the VFU. I'm also raising VFU lanes to 64 and the star units to 16, keeping lean tiles so area stays under 3000 mm2.

Design #5 is the only fast point but is 5833 mm2, over the 3000 mm2 limit. Crossbar arrays are likely the dominant area term, so I halve xbar_scale to 0.5 while keeping the fast mapping (xbar MVM/LM head/attention, transpose tech, star softmax, die link, 8-bit KV). I also reduce VFU lanes from 64 to 16 to recover more area, with the VFU memory at 16G/256G as in the feasible #3 point. This tests whether the crossbar scale can be cut without a large time penalty.

Evaluation #5 (xbar attention, transpose, star softmax, lean tiles, scale 1.0) gave the big speedup (506 s) but overshot area at 5833 mm2, while #6 at scale 0.5 ran out of KV room. This point tries the middle: xbar_scale 0.75 for enough capacity, adc_per_ima 2 to cut tile area by about 31%, and kv_bits 8 to halve KV footprint, keeping the fast xbar-attention/star path.

Design #5 was fast (506 s) but 5833 mm2 over budget, and shrinking xbar_scale below 1.0 breaks context capacity. Keeping xbar_scale 1.0 and cutting area with adc_per_ima 2 (-31% tile area) and cell_bits 4 (half the arrays at 1.27x area each, about 0.64x total) should bring the #5 architecture under 3000 mm2 without losing capacity. This is an unevaluated point that tests whether the fast attention-on-crossbar design can be made feasible.

Feasible best so far is #8 (843.5 s, 2460 mm2), which trades ADC count and cell bits for area. Changing only adc_per_ima from 2 to 4 tests whether the read-latency penalty is a bottleneck worth the area, since #5 (adc 8, cell 2) reached 506 s at 5833 mm2. If the area stays under 3000 mm2, this is a clean intermediate point on the ADC-area curve.

Design #9 is the best feasible point so far (632.6 s, 2871 mm2, just under the 3000 mm2 limit). I'll route the elementwise vector ops to the fixed-function star unit instead of the VFU, and drop VFU lanes from 64 to 16 to recover area for that unit. This tests whether the vector-op path is a bottleneck and whether the VFU lanes are oversized.

Design #10 (570 s, 2871 mm2) is the best feasible point, and its area is close to the limit. Lowering xbar_scale to 0.75 should free area, and with cell_bits=4 the effective capacity should still cover the longest context (the earlier out-of-room failures used cell_bits=2). The freed area can go to star_units=64, which speeds up the star softmax and vector work that dominate the remaining time.

Best feasible so far is #10 (570 s, area 2871 mm2), where softmax and vector both run on star units but only 16 star instances are used. Reducing xbar_scale below 1.0 has repeatedly hit "out of room" limits, so I'll keep xbar_scale at 1.0 and test whether more nonlinear throughput (star_units 64) helps, accepting the area risk near the 3000 mm2 limit.

Best feasible so far is #12 (525.2 s, 2872 mm2), sitting just under the area cap with little headroom. The untested lever with the biggest potential area saving is moving lm_head to the CPU, since the vocabulary projection occupies a large share of crossbars. I'll change only that knob from #12 to measure its area and time effect, which could free area for a higher ADC count or crossbar scale.

Best feasible so far is #12 (525.2 s, 2872 mm2), with only about 128 mm2 of headroom. Moving edge (embedding and sampling) from vfu to cpu is a small change that may free area from the vector unit and show whether edge placement matters for time. It keeps every other knob from the best design.

The best feasible point so far is #12 (525 s, 2872 mm2), and it sits right at the area limit, so shrinking the crossbar budget is not an option (scale 0.75 failed on context capacity). Attention on the crossbars is what made those designs fast, but it also forces xbar_scale 1.0 and consumes most of the area. Attention on the VFU with a large, fast KV memory (256 lanes, 1 TB/s, 64 GB) and star softmax is untested and may need less crossbar capacity, which would free area for finer ADCs or cell settings.

Best feasible so far is #12 (525.2 s, 2872 mm2), and the comparison of #13 vs #14 shows lm_head and mvm on xbar matter most. With vector and softmax on star, the VFU only handles edge work, so I'll move edge to CPU and drop vfu_units to 4 to test whether that frees area without hurting time.

Best feasible so far is #12 (525.2 s, 2872 mm2), where star units and star vector ops helped most. Moving edge from vfu to cpu is an untested single change from that point: it may cut area or remove a sampling/embedding bottleneck, and it isolates whether the edge vfu is contributing to time.

Best feasible so far is #12 (525.2 s, 2872 mm2), with star_units 64 and vector star helping most. Next I test whether vfu_units can drop from 16 to 4 without hurting time, since that frees area for later crossbar or ADC trade-offs. This point differs from all evaluated designs.

Best feasible so far is #12 (525.2 s, area 2872). Holding the xbar/ADC/star/vector settings fixed, the remaining untested knob that could change time is edge (embedding and sampling on CPU instead of VFU), which should be area-neutral. This tests whether moving those tiny ops off the VFU helps, and it costs one evaluation.

Best feasible so far is #12 (525.2 s, 2872 mm2). Area looks dominated by crossbar size and ADC/tile choices, not by star or VFU lanes (#9, #10, #12, #16 all sit at about 2872 mm2). Trading ADCs from 4 to 2 frees tile area, and I can spend some of that on xbar_scale 1.25, which could cut time if extra arrays add parallelism. This combination has not been evaluated.

Best feasible so far is #12 (525.2 s, 2872 mm2), and it is area-limited, so adc 8 or larger xbar_scale won't fit. The remaining unexplored knob in that configuration is edge, which I haven't tested with cpu under the star/xbar stack. Moving edge to cpu may free area from the VFU embedding/sampling path and shows whether that work is on the critical path.

Best feasible so far is #12 (525.2 s, 2872 mm2), which uses edge=vfu. Moving the embedding and sampling to the CPU (edge=cpu) is the one unexplored knob in that otherwise-best configuration, and it may cut area from the vector unit while changing time only slightly.

Best feasible so far is #12 (525 s, 2872 mm2), but the ADC=2 variant (#17) overshot area at 3076 mm2 with lm_head on xbar. Moving the vocabulary projection to CPU should free crossbar area, so adc_per_ima=2 may fit under 3000 mm2 while keeping the star/xbar attention path that drives the speedup. This tests an untried area-recovery combination.

Best feasible so far is #12 (525 s, 2872 mm2), and xbar_scale 1.0 is the minimum that holds long contexts when attention stays on xbar. Moving attention to vfu with a 16G KV memory removes the xbar KV burden, so xbar_scale can drop to 0.75 and xbar_transpose (+15% area) is unnecessary, freeing area for a faster configuration.

Best feasible so far is #12 at 525 s with area 2872, and the crossbar arrays drive area. Attention on the vector unit with 256 lanes, 1 TB/s and 64 GB KV memory gave tiny area (691 mm2) but failed at 1 token, both times at xbar_scale 0.75. Testing the same attention-VFU setup at xbar_scale 1.0 checks whether that failure was the scale and whether this route can beat 525 s within the area budget.

The best feasible point so far is #12 (525.2 s, 2872 mm2), and the area margin there is small, so most knobs are near their limits. The untested lever with plausible time or area benefit is edge on CPU instead of the VFU. Effort is not part of the objective, so it can be ignored when choosing.

Best feasible so far is #12 (525.2 s, 2872 mm2, 22 mo). Area is dominated by crossbars (xbar_scale 1.0 is pinned by feasibility), so I'm testing the untried edge=cpu on the #12 base. This keeps effort at 22 mo and checks whether embedding/sampling on the CPU beats the vector unit.

Best feasible designs cluster around attention=xbar, vector=star, softmax=star, adc 4, cell 4 (~525 s, 2872 mm2). Changing only lm_head to cpu from #12 is an unevaluated point that tests whether the LM-head crossbars are worth their area; if area drops a lot, the freed budget can go to adc/xbar_scale in later steps.

Best feasible so far is #12 (525.2 s, 2872 mm2), where area is nearly saturated by ADCs and star units. Trying xbar_scale 1.25 with adc_per_ima 2 and star_units 16 is untested. Its area should land near #8's 2460 mm2 plus the added arrays, and it tests whether extra crossbar capacity buys time without the ADC penalty.

Best feasible is #12 (525.2 s, 2872 mm2). Attention-on-crossbar, lm_head on crossbar, star softmax/vector, and cell 4 with adc 4 are all established. Moving edge (embedding lookup and sampling) to the CPU is untested and adds no area or effort, so it is the cheapest next probe.

Best feasible so far is #12 (525.2 s, 2872 mm2), which is close to the area cap, so area-adding knobs like xbar_scale 1.25 or adc 8 are likely infeasible. Edge is the one knob in the best config never tested on its own, and moving embedding and sampling to CPU might free VFU work without raising area. I'm keeping the #12 settings otherwise, so this isolates the edge effect.

Best feasible so far is #12 (525.2 s, 2872 mm2), and the lm_head and attention on crossbars drive most of the gain. Scaling crossbars to 1.25x with the #12 settings (adc 4, cell 4) is untested and tells me whether extra arrays cut the LLM time enough to justify the area, which is the main open trade-off.

Best feasible so far is #12 (525.2 s, 2872 mm2), which keeps the ADC at 4 and the cell at 4 bits. Scale 1.0 is the lowest feasible value, and the bigger levers (lm_head, mvm, attention, softmax/vector on star) are already set. Moving edge from vfu to cpu is the one untested knob on the current best. It should cost almost no area, since VFU and star units barely moved area in earlier runs, and it tests whether the embedding and sampling work is actually on the critical path.

Best feasible so far is #12 (525.2 s, 2872 mm2), and #22 shows the 1.25 default crossbar scale is what pushed area to 3589. The one untested knob in that feasible configuration is edge, so I'll move the embedding and sampling back to the CPU and keep everything else as in #12 to see whether it changes time or area.

Best feasible so far is #12 (525.2 s, 2872 mm2), where star_units=64 helped most. Going from adc 4 to adc 2 cut area by about 513 mm2 at xbar_scale 1.25 (#17 vs #22), so at xbar_scale 1.0 it should fit well under 3000. This point is untested and tests whether the ADC-bound read latency is offset by the smaller array area.

Best feasible is #12 at ~525 s (area 2872). Edge-on-VFU costs ~700 mm2 for negligible gain, so keep edge on CPU. Lowering ADCs from 4 to 2 cost ~200 s, so testing 8 ADCs per IMA (with lean tile, 4-bit cells, scale 1.0) measures how much ADC throughput is still limiting; it will likely exceed area, but it tells us whether a cheaper way to add ADC throughput is worth finding.

Best feasible is about 525 s (#12, area 2872), and ADC count is the main lever: 2→4 ADCs cut time from 843 to 632 s. Going to 8 ADCs should speed up reads further, but it likely overshoots the area cap. Moving the vocabulary projection back to the CPU frees the crossbars it occupies, so this tests whether that offsets the ADC area.

Best feasible so far is #12 (525 s, 2872 mm2), and #24 hints that edge=cpu with vfu_units=1 ran faster (420 s) even though its area was over budget. xbar_scale 1.0 is the lowest value that fits the context length and adds no time benefit above that, so I keep it. This point tests edge=cpu with vfu_units=1 at xbar_scale 1.0 to see if it cuts time while staying under 3000 mm2.

Best feasible so far is #12 (525.2 s, 2872 mm2), and it sits close to the 3000 mm2 limit. Switching the crossbar flavor to xbar_isaac saves roughly 15% of crossbar area, which could bring the design well under the limit while keeping ADC=4 and the 1.0 crossbar scale that avoids the long-context failures. This is a point not yet evaluated and tests whether the K-append penalty is small enough to trade for area.

Best feasible so far is #12 (525.2 s, 2872 mm2), where ADC count is the main lever: adc 2 costs about 200 s and saves about 410 mm2, so adc 8 would be faster but too large. Star units and vfu lanes add almost no area, so the way to make room for more ADCs is to remove area elsewhere. Testing lm_head on CPU with adc 8 measures whether the vocabulary-projection crossbars are a large enough area share to fund the extra ADCs.

Best feasible so far is #12 (525.2 s, area 2872 mm2), which is near the area limit. I'll test whether moving the vocabulary projection to CPU frees enough area to afford 8 ADCs per IMA, which should speed up crossbar reads. This combination is untested and may be infeasible on area, but it is the most informative step from the current best.

Best feasible so far is #12 (525.2 s, 2872 mm2), which is close to the area limit. Its edge work runs on the VFU, and I have not tested edge=cpu with this otherwise-best configuration. Moving edge to the CPU might free area for little time cost, since the embedding lookup and sampling are small.

The transpose-tech designs with adc 4 sit at about 525 s but near 2872 mm2, and adc 8 cannot fit there. Evaluation #26 (xbar_isaac, adc 4) came in at only 2023 mm2, leaving roughly 900 mm2 of headroom. This probe spends that headroom on adc 8 to test whether faster ADC reads can cut the isaac attention time enough to be competitive, and it has not been evaluated before.

Best feasible so far is #12 (525.2 s, 2872 mm2). Area is driven mainly by xbar_scale (1.0 is the minimum that fits the weights and context), by adc_per_ima, and by xbar_tech (transpose adds about 850 mm2 over isaac). Area barely moves with vfu_units or star_units. adc 8 would be faster (420 s) but is about 820 mm2 over budget, and attention on vfu is roughly 10x slower, so the remaining gains are small. I'll test the one untried neighbor of #12 that keeps area essentially fixed, raising vfu_units from 16 to 64 with edge on vfu.

Best feasible so far is #12/#28 at ~525 s with area 2872 mm2. Area is near the limit, so I need an untested change that could cut time without adding area. Edge is the one knob not yet tried on the best point: #24 was fastest (420 s) with edge on CPU, while every feasible design with edge on VFU sits near 525 s. Moving edge to CPU and dropping VFU lanes to 1 should save a little area (VFU lane count barely affected area in #16) and tests whether the edge-on-VFU choice is what costs time.

Best feasible so far is about 525 s (#12/#28, area 2872), and area is driven mainly by crossbars and ADCs. The only untested knob in that near-frontier configuration is kv_bits=16, so I'll check whether KV precision changes time or area there.

Best feasible so far is #12 (525.2 s, 2872 mm2), and time is driven mainly by the crossbar read speed (adc_per_ima), which was capped at 4 by area. Switching to xbar_tech isaac removes about 15% of crossbar area, which may leave room for adc_per_ima 8 (2x faster reads) at scale 1.0 with the rest of the #12 configuration.

Area is dominated by crossbars and ADCs, and xbar_transpose adds about 15% area. Swapping to xbar_isaac (adc 4, cell 4, lean tile, kv 8, star 64, vfu 16, edge vfu, lm_head xbar) should free roughly 350 mm2, which might allow a larger crossbar scale (1.25) for more parallelism. This combination has not been evaluated, and it tests whether the transpose-tech area cost can be traded for speed.

Feasible best so far is about 525 s at area 2872, and the lowest workload seen (420.5 s, #24) was infeasible only because of area (3692) at adc_per_ima=8. Dropping adc to 4 should cut the area back under 3000, since adc=4 at scale 1.0 gave about 2872 in #12. Keeping edge on the CPU, as in #24, tests whether the faster #24 runtime comes from that choice rather than from the ADC count.

Best feasible so far is #12 at 525 s (area 2872), limited by ADC read time, while the adc=8 variant (#24) reaches 420 s but overshoots area at 3692. Trying xbar_isaac (about 15% less crossbar area than transpose) with adc=8, cell=4, lean tile, and minimal VFU/star units tests whether the ADC-heavy design can fit under 3000 mm2. This point has not been evaluated.

Best feasible so far is about 525 s (#12/#28), limited by ADC count: adc 4 at scale 1.0 uses ~2872 mm2, and adc 2 is clearly slower (736 s). xbar_scale 1.0 is the smallest context-safe value, and scale barely changes time, so the remaining lever is more ADCs. Moving lm_head to CPU should free xbar area, which could make adc 8 fit under 3000 mm2 and may speed up the attention and MVM reads. This tests whether adc 8 plus a smaller crossbar footprint beats the current frontier.

The best feasible points (#12, #28) sit at about 525 s with area 2872, and ADC count is the main remaining time lever: going from 2 to 4 ADCs cut time by about 1.33x. ADC 8 at xbar_scale 1.0 with cell_bits 4 is untested and may exceed the area cap, but it is the most informative next step. Effort does not enter the objective, so the other knobs stay as in #12.

Best feasible so far is about 525 s (#12, #28) at adc 4. Evals #24 and #32 reached 420 s with adc 8, but they left xbar_scale at the start value of 1.25, which is why they came out at 3692 mm2. Area scales roughly linearly with xbar_scale (about 2870 mm2 at 1.0 vs 3589 at 1.25 for adc 4), so scaling 3692 mm2 back to 1.0 gives roughly 2950 mm2, which fits under 3000. This tests the untried combination of adc 8, cell 4, transpose and xbar_scale 1.0.

The best feasible designs sit near 525 s at about 2872 mm2, and the area cap is the binding constraint. No evaluation has yet paired attention=xbar with xbar_tech=xbar_isaac. Isaac's smaller arrays (about 15% less area) could bring the design under the cap while keeping adc_per_ima=4 and cell_bits=4, so this tests whether that trade is worthwhile.

Best feasible region is #12 (525.2 s, 2872 mm2), which sits near the area limit and the tools floor is 227 s. Changing only edge from vfu to cpu is an unexplored neighbor that may free area from the VFU-side edge logic without hurting the rest of the pipeline, so it is the most informative next step.

The best feasible point so far is #12/#28 at about 525 s with 2872 mm2, and time looks floored by crossbar read latency, so ADC count and cell size are the remaining levers. Area is dominated by crossbars and ADCs, and 4-bit cells cost time on row writes. Trying 2-bit cells with 2 ADCs per IMA (cheaper ADCs, and faster writes with no write-verify) at the minimum feasible xbar_scale 1.0 is an untested point that could beat 525 s if the area stays under 3000.
